drivingQuestion: Which objects placed against a ten-handbreadth wall reduce it so that it functions as an opening between two courtyards?
outcomeNote: A cluster of amoraic rulings; the closing dilemma is answered by Rabba, challenged by Rav Ḥisda, and Rav Ḥisda is supported by an איתמר נמי tradition; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak records a variant framing.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּסוּלָּם הַמִּצְרִי דְּלָא מְמַעֵט? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר רַב: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ דָּבָר שֶׁנִּיטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת, וְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּיטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת — אֵינוֹ מְמַעֵט.
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: What is the reason» that «an Egyptian ladder does not diminish» the height of a wall? He «said to him: Did you not hear» that which «Rav Aḥa bar Adda said» that «Rav Hamnuna said» that «Rav said:» It is «because it is an object that may be moved on Shabbat,» i.e., it is not set-aside [muktze], «and» the principle is that «any object that may be moved on Shabbat does not diminish» the height of a wall, as it cannot be considered a permanent part of the wall.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ צוֹרִי נָמֵי! הָתָם כּוֹבְדוֹ קוֹבְעוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «If so,» this should apply «even» to «a Tyrian» ladder «as well,» as a large ladder is also not set-aside and may be handled on Shabbat. The Gemara answers: «There,» in the case of a Tyrian ladder, «its heaviness establishes it» as part of the wall. Even though one is permitted to move it, since due to its weight it is not moved easily, it effectively diminishes the height of the wall.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כּוֹתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְהִנִּיחַ סוּלָּם רָחָב אַרְבָּעָה מִכָּאן וְסוּלַּם רָחָב אַרְבָּעָה מִכָּאן, וְאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים — מְמַעֵט. שְׁלֹשָׁה — אֵינוֹ מְמַעֵט.
segments.en: «Abaye said:» If «a wall between two courtyards» is «ten handbreadths high, and one placed a ladder four» handbreadths «wide» against the wall «on one side,» in one courtyard, «and» another «ladder four» handbreadths «wide on the other side,» in the other courtyard, «and there are less than three handbreadths between them,» i.e., the two ladders on the opposite sides of the wall are within three handbreadths of each other, even if they are not directly opposite each other, this «diminishes» the height of the wall. The pair of ladders is regarded as a valid passageway between the two courtyards. However, if the gap between the two ladders is «three» handbreadths or more, this «does not diminish» the height of the wall.

segments.he: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא הָוֵי כּוֹתֶל אַרְבָּעָה, אֲבָל הָוֵי כּוֹתֶל אַרְבָּעָה — אֲפִילּוּ מוּפְלָג טוּבָא, נָמֵי.
segments.en: «And we only said» this qualification if the «wall was less than four» handbreadths wide. However, «if» the «wall was» at least «four» handbreadths wide, then «even» if one ladder was «greatly distanced» from the other, this «likewise» renders it permitted. Since it is possible to walk along the thickness of the wall, the pair of ladders constitutes a passageway between the two courtyards.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: בָּנָה אִיצְטְבָא עַל גַּב אִיצְטְבָא, אִם יֵשׁ בָּאִיצְטְבָא הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה — מְמַעֵט. אִי נָמֵי אֵין בַּתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה, וְיֵשׁ בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה, וְאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה — מְמַעֵט.
segments.en: «Rav Beivai bar Abaye said: If one built a» wooden «platform» next to the wall «above» another «platform,» then «if the lower platform is four» handbreadths wide, «it diminishes» the height of the wall to below ten handbreadths. «Alternatively,» if «the lower» one «is not four» handbreadths wide, «but the upper» one «is four» handbreadths wide, «and there is» a gap of «less than three» handbreadths «between them, it diminishes» the height of the wall, as the two platforms are considered as one.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: סוּלָּם שֶׁשְּׁלִיבוֹתָיו פּוֹרְחוֹת, אִם יֵשׁ בַּשְּׁלִיבָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה — מְמַעֵט. אִי נָמֵי אֵין בַּשְּׁלִיבָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה וְיֵשׁ בַּשְּׁלִיבָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה, וְאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה — מְמַעֵט.
segments.en: «And Rav Naḥman said» that «Rabba bar Avuh said:» In the case of «a ladder whose rungs are disconnected, if the bottom rung is four» handbreadths wide, «it diminishes» the height of the wall. «Alternatively,» if «the bottom rung is not four» handbreadths wide, «but the upper rung is four» handbreadths wide, «and there is» a gap of «less than three» handbreadths «between them, it diminishes» the height of the wall, because the principle of lavud joins the two rungs together.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
segments.en: «And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:»

segments.he: זִיז הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַכּוֹתֶל אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה, וְהִנִּיחַ עָלָיו סוּלָּם כׇּל שֶׁהוּא — מִיעֲטוֹ.
segments.en: If «a projection four by four» handbreadths in area «extends from a wall, and one placed a ladder of any» width «against it,» if the rungs of the ladder are less than three handbreadths apart, «he has diminished» the height of the wall by means of this ladder and projection.

segments.he: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּאוֹתְבֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ, אֲבָל אוֹתְבֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ אַרְווֹחֵי אַרְוְחֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara qualifies this statement: «And we said» this «only» in a case «where one placed» the ladder directly «against» the projection, so that the ladder serves as a passage to it. «However, if he placed it adjacent to» the projection, «he has» merely «widened» the projection, while the ladder remains separate from it. Consequently, the projection does not have any connection to the ground, and a projection that is not within three handbreadths of the ground does not diminish the height of a wall.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: כּוֹתֶל תִּשְׁעָה עָשָׂר — צָרִיךְ זִיז אֶחָד לְהַתִּירוֹ.
segments.en: «And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:» If «a wall» between two courtyards is «nineteen» handbreadths high, «it requires one projection to» render the use of the wall «permitted.» If there is a single projection in the middle of the wall, with a ladder of any width resting against it, it is considered a passageway between the courtyards, as the projection is within ten handbreadths of the top of the wall.

segments.he: כּוֹתֶל עֶשְׂרִים — צָרִיךְ שְׁנֵי זִיזִים לְהַתִּירוֹ. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וְהוּא שֶׁהֶעֱמִידָן זֶה שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה.
segments.en: However, if «the wall» is «twenty» handbreadths high, it «requires two projections to» render the use of the wall «permitted,» one within ten handbreadths of the ground, and the other within ten handbreadths of the top of the wall. «Rav Ḥisda said: And this» applies only «where he positioned» the projections «not» directly «one above the other,» so that it is possible to use a ladder to climb from one projection to the other.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עַמּוּד בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה וְרָחָב אַרְבָּעָה, וְנָעַץ בּוֹ יָתֵד כׇּל שֶׁהוּא — מִיעֲטוֹ.
segments.en: «Rav Huna said:» If «a pillar in the public domain» is «ten» handbreadths «high and four» handbreadths «wide,» so that it is considered a private domain, «and one drove a stake of any» size «into» the top of «it, he has diminished its» area. The usable area is now less than four handbreadths, and therefore the pillar is no longer considered a private domain.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וּבְגָבוֹהַּ שְׁלֹשָׁה. אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁלֹשָׁה.
segments.en: «Rav Adda bar Ahava said:» This applies only if the stake is at least «three» handbreadths «high.» If it is less than three handbreadths high, it is considered part of the top of the pillar, based on the principle of lavud. This is in contrast to «Abaye and Rava, who both say: Even if» the stake is «not three» handbreadths «high,» the pillar is no longer considered a private domain.

segments.he: מַאי טַעְמָא: לָא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «What is the reason» for the opinion of Abaye and Rava? It is that the pillar «is no longer» fit to be «used,» as a surface of four by four handbreadths is suitable for use only when it is level. If it has even a small projection, it is no longer usable.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁגָּבוֹהַּ שְׁלֹשָׁה, מַאי טַעְמָא: אֶפְשָׁר דְּתָלֵי בֵּיהּ מִידֵּי.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: Even a stake three» handbreadths «high» does not diminish the area of the pillar. «What is the reason» for this? It is that «it is possible to hang an item on it. Although» it is no longer possible to rest objects on top of the pillar, it is still useful in some way.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מִלְּאוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בִּיתֵדוֹת מַהוּ?
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:» According to your opinion, if «he filled it entirely with stakes,» i.e., if he drove so many stakes into the top of the post that it was completely filled, «what is» the halakha?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בּוֹר וְחוּלְיָיתָהּ מִצְטָרֵף לַעֲשָׂרָה.
segments.en: Rav Ashi «said to him: Did you not hear that» which «Rabbi Yoḥanan said?» He said that «a pit and its embankment» of stone around the edge «join» together to complete the measure of «ten» handbreadths. Similarly, the width of the embankment joins with the diameter of the pit to complete the measure of four by four handbreadths necessary to define the pit as a private domain.

segments.he: וְאַמַּאי, הָא לָא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לֵיהּ? אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר — דְּמַנַּח מִידֵּי וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ, הָכָא נָמֵי דְּמַנַּח מִידֵּי וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ.
segments.en: There, too, one can raise the question: «But why? He cannot use» the embankment, as most of the area is the empty space of the pit. «Rather, what have you to say,» i.e., how can you solve this problem? The solution is «that he places an item,» e.g., a board, over the mouth of the pit, «and» then he can make «use» of it. «Here, too, he places an item» over the stakes «and» can make «use» of the pillar.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כּוֹתֶל עֲשָׂרָה — צָרִיךְ סוּלָּם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר לְהַתִּירוֹ. רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר וּמַשֶּׁהוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said:» If «a wall» is «ten» handbreadths high, «it requires a ladder fourteen» handbreadths high, so that one can place the ladder at a diagonal against the wall. The ladder then functions as a passageway and thereby renders the use of the wall «permitted. Rav Yosef said: Even» a ladder with a height of «thirteen» handbreadths «and a bit» is enough, as it is sufficient if the ladder reaches within one handbreadth of the top of the wall.

segments.he: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אַחַד עָשָׂר וּמַשֶּׁהוּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said: Even» a ladder that is only «eleven» handbreadths «and a bit» suffices, as the ladder will still reach a height of over seven handbreadths, i.e., within three handbreadths of the top of the wall.

segments.he: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שִׁבְעָה וּמַשֶּׁהוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said: Even» if the ladder is only «seven» handbreadths «and a bit» it is sufficient, as he can stand the ladder upright against the wall. Since it will reach within three handbreadths of the top of the wall, the principle of lavud applies. Therefore, even a ladder placed in this manner is considered a valid passageway between the two courtyards.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב: סוּלָּם זָקוּף — מְמַעֵט. גְּמָרָא, וְלָא יָדַעְנָא מַאי טַעְמָא.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rav said: An upright ladder» effectively «diminishes» the height of a wall, as it creates a passageway. I received this teaching as «a tradition, but I do not know what the reason is,» as people do not generally climb ladders positioned in this manner.

segments.he: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְלָא יָדַע אַבָּא טַעְמָא דְּהָא מִלְּתָא?! מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַאִיצְטְבָא עַל גַּבֵּי אִיצְטְבָא.
segments.en: «Shmuel said: Does Abba,» i.e., Rav, actually «not know the reason for this matter?» The reason here is «just as it is» in the case of «a platform above» another «platform.» Even though it is not easy to climb, since it provides steps that can be climbed, albeit with difficulty, it is considered a valid passageway.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: דְּקָלִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל — אֵינָן צְרִיכִין קֶבַע. מַאי טַעְמָא: כְּבֵידָן קוֹבַעְתָּן.
segments.en: «Rabba said» that «Rabbi Ḥiyya said:» The trunks of «palm trees in Babylonia» that were placed next to a wall between two courtyards so that people could climb on them and pass from one courtyard to another «do not need to be established» permanently and attached to the ground; rather, they serve to diminish the wall as they are. «What is the reason» for this? It is that «their heaviness establishes them» as connected to the ground. Although it is permitted to handle them, nevertheless, since their weight makes them difficult to move, they are considered fixed in place.

segments.he: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: סוּלָּמוֹת שֶׁבְּבָבֶל — אֵינָן צְרִיכִין קֶבַע. מַאי טַעְמָא: כְּבֵידָן קוֹבַעְתָּן.
segments.en: «And» similarly, «Rav Yosef» said that «Rabbi Oshaya said: Ladders in Babylonia do not need» to be «established» and fixed permanently in place. «What is the reason» for this? It is that «their heaviness establishes them,» as the ladders in Babylonia were typically large and heavy.

segments.he: מַאן דְּאָמַר סוּלָּמוֹת, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּקָלִים. וּמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּקָלִים, אֲבָל סוּלָּמוֹת לָא.
segments.en: The Gemara comments: With regard to «the one who said» that Babylonian «ladders» do not need to be fixed in place, «all the more so» would he agree that the trunks of «palm trees,» which are placed there from the outset for this purpose, are considered fixed, as both are extremely heavy and also designed to remain in place. On the other hand, «the one who said» that the trunks of «palm trees» need not be fixed permanently in the ground, spoke only with regard to palm trees. «However,» as for «ladders, no,» they are not considered fixed in place. A ladder, even a heavy one, is designed to be moved from place to place.

segments.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מֵרַבָּה: סוּלָּם מִכָּאן וְסוּלָּם מִכָּאן וְקַשִּׁין בָּאֶמְצַע, מַהוּ?
segments.en: «Rav Yosef raised a dilemma before Rabba:» If there is a narrow «ladder» measuring less than two handbreadths wide «on one» side, «and a» similarly narrow «ladder on the other» side, «and» there are rungs of woven «straw in the middle» between them which would not support a person’s weight, «what is» the halakha? Are the two ladders considered a single unit, forming a ladder four handbreadths wide, which serves to diminish the height of a wall?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין כַּף הָרֶגֶל עוֹלָה בָּהֶן.
segments.en: Rabba «said to him: The sole of the foot cannot» climb «upon them.» A person usually places his foot in the middle of a ladder. Since the middle of this ladder is made of straw, then although it appears to be four handbreadths wide, it is not fit for use and does not diminish the height of the wall.

segments.he: קַשִּׁין מִכָּאן וְקַשִּׁין מִכָּאן וְסוּלָּם בָּאֶמְצַע, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי כַּף הָרֶגֶל עוֹלָה בָּהֶן.
segments.en: Rav Yosef continued to ask: And what if there were rungs of «straw on one» side «and» rungs of «straw on the other» side, «and a» narrow «ladder» less than four handbreadths wide «in the middle,» and their combined width is four handbreadths? «What is» the halakha in this case? Rabba «said to him: The sole of the foot can» climb «upon them,» and the ladder appears to be four handbreadths wide. Therefore, it serves to diminish the height of the wall.

segments.he: חָקַק לְהַשְׁלִים בַּכּוֹתֶל, בְּכַמָּה? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּעֲשָׂרָה.
segments.en: Rav Yosef further asked: If the ladder resting against the wall was less than four handbreadths wide, and «one dug out» grooves «in the wall» as extensions of the rungs of the ladder «to complete» the measure, «how» high must this hollowed-out section be to consider the ladder a valid passageway between the two courtyards? Rabba «said to him:» If it is «ten» handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide, it is considered a passageway.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲקָקוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בַּכּוֹתֶל, בְּכַמָּה? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְלֹא קוֹמָתוֹ. וּמַאי שְׁנָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם מִסְתַּלֵּק לֵיהּ, הָכָא לָא מִסְתַּלֵּק לֵיהּ.
segments.en: Rav Yosef «said to him:» If there was no ladder, and «one dug out the entire» ladder «in the wall,» so that all the steps are grooves in the wall, «how much» must he hollow out? Rabba «said to him:» Those steps must reach «the full height of» the wall. Rav Yosef asked: «And what is the difference» in this case? Why must the steps reach higher in this case than in the case where the hollowed-out section was merely an extension of an existing ladder? Rabba «said to him: There,» where there is a ladder, «it is easy to climb» to the top of the wall; however, «here,» where there are only grooves in the wall, «it is not easy to climb.» If one cannot reach the top of the wall, the steps are not considered a passageway between the courtyards.

segments.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מֵרַבָּה: עֲשָׂאוֹ לָאִילָן סוּלָּם, מַהוּ?
segments.en: «Rav Yosef raised a dilemma before Rabba: If one designated a tree as a ladder, what is» the halakha? Given that it is prohibited to climb a tree on Shabbat, if a tree stands next to a wall and it is easy to climb, is it considered with regard to the halakhot of Shabbat as an opening in the wall that can serve as a passageway between the two courtyards?

segments.he: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי, תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: «Let the dilemma be raised» according «to» the opinion of «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi, who maintains that a joining of Shabbat boundaries [eiruv teḥumin] placed in a tree is valid; and «let the dilemma be raised» according «to» the opinion of «the Rabbis,» who disagree.

segments.he: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת לֹא גָּזְרוּ עָלָיו — הָנֵי מִילֵּי בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, אֲבָל כּוּלֵּי יוֹמָא — לָא.
segments.en: The Gemara elaborates: «Let the dilemma be raised» according «to» the previously stated opinion of «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi. «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «only stated there» that with regard to «anything that is» prohibited on Shabbat «due to a rabbinic decree [shevut],» the Sages «did not prohibit» it during twilight. Therefore, in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s opinion, it is permitted to use an eiruv that was deposited in a tree, as the use of a tree is prohibited on Shabbat by rabbinic decree. However, «this applies only» in that case, as the eiruv takes effect «during the twilight period.» Since there is doubt with regard to whether that period is considered day or night, the decree is not in force, and the eiruv is therefore valid. «However,» in this case, where the opening must be valid for «the entire day,» Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi would «not» rule that the decree does not apply. Since it is prohibited by rabbinic decree to climb a tree on Shabbat, a tree cannot be considered a valid passageway.

segments.he: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן: פִּיתְחָא הוּא, וְאַרְיָא הוּא דִּרְבִיעַ עֲלֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Or perhaps» it may be argued that «even according to» the opinion of «the Rabbis,» this tree is considered an opening. They may have said that a joining of Shabbat boundaries placed in a tree is not valid only because the eiruv must actually be accessible during twilight, and in that case it is not, due to the rabbinic decree. However, in this case, where it is not necessary to make actual use of the tree, they would agree that a tree that serves as a ladder «is a» valid «entrance, but a lion crouches upon it.» Just as a lion crouching at an opening does not thereby nullify its status as an entrance, although in practice no one can pass through it, so too, in the case of the tree, the prohibition against climbing it does not nullify its status as a passageway.

segments.he: עֲשָׂאוֹ לַאֲשֵׁירָה סוּלָּם, מַהוּ? תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: Rav Yosef further inquired: «If one designated a tree worshipped as part of idolatrous rites [asheira],» from which it is forbidden to derive benefit, «as a ladder, what is» the halakha? Is it considered a valid passageway in the wall with regard to the halakhot of Shabbat? Here, too, «let the dilemma be raised» according «to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda,» and «let the dilemma be raised» according «to» the opinion of «the Rabbis.»

segments.he: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם דְּמוּתָּר לִקְנוֹת בַּיִת בְּאִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה, אֶלָּא הָתָם, דְּבָתַר דִּקְנָה לֵיהּ עֵירוּב לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלִינְּטַר.
segments.en: The Gemara elaborates: «Let the dilemma be raised» according «to» the previously stated opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yehuda only stated there» that «it is permitted to acquire,» i.e., make use of, «a house» for the purposes of establishing an eiruv even if it is among the «items» from which it is «prohibited to» derive «benefit,» such as a grave. This statement applies only «there,» with regard to acquiring an eiruv in that location, «since after the eiruv has acquired» a place of residence «for him, it is not important to him that it is guarded.» He requires the grave only for the moment of the acquisition of the eiruv, and what happens to it afterward is of no consequence to him. However, here, since one desires the continued presence of the ladder, it is possible that even Rabbi Yehuda would agree that one may not rely on an asheira, as one may not climb and make use of it, since it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

segments.he: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן: פִּיתְחָא הוּא, וְאַרְיָא דִּרְבִיעַ עֲלֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Or perhaps» it may be argued that «even» though according «to» the opinion of «the Rabbis» it is prohibited to use a grave to acquire an eiruv, here they would agree that the asheira «is an opening, but a lion crouches upon it,» and this does not nullify its status as an opening.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִילָן מוּתָּר, וַאֲשֵׁירָה אֲסוּרָה. מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִילָן שֶׁאִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת גּוֹרֵם לוֹ — נִיתְּסַר.
segments.en: Rabba «said to him: A tree is permitted» for use as a ladder, «but an asheira is prohibited. Rav Ḥisda strongly objects to this: On the contrary, a tree,» with regard to «which a Shabbat prohibition causes it» to be prohibited, «should be prohibited,» so that it will not be said that a Shabbat prohibition has been disregarded in a case involving the halakhot of Shabbat.

segments.he: אֲשֵׁירָה שֶׁאִיסּוּר דָּבָר אַחֵר גּוֹרֵם לוֹ — לָא נִיתְּסַר.
segments.en: And the converse is also true: «An asheira,» with regard to «which something else,» a halakha unrelated to the halakhot of Shabbat, «causes it» to be prohibited, «should not be prohibited.» Rather, it should be considered an opening with regard to Shabbat.

segments.he: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כֹּל שֶׁאִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת גָּרַם לוֹ — אָסוּר, כֹּל שֶׁאִיסּוּר דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לוֹ — מוּתָּר.
segments.en: Indeed, «it was also stated: When Ravin came» from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia, he said that «Rabbi Elazar said, and some say» that «Rabbi Abbahu said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Anything» with regard to «which a prohibition of Shabbat causes it» to be prohibited «is prohibited;» and conversely, «anything» with regard to «which something else causes it» to be prohibited «is permitted.»

segments.he: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי: אִילָן — פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי וְרַבָּנַן. אֲשֵׁירָה — פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: However, in contrast to Rav Yosef, «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak taught as follows:» These questions are indeed dependent on the known disputes. Whether «a tree» serving as a ladder constitutes a valid opening «is» the subject of «a dispute» between «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «and the Rabbis;» Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi permits it and the Rabbis prohibit it. The debate with regard to whether or not «an asheira» is considered an opening «is» the subject of «a dispute» between «Rabbi Yehuda,» who permits using items from which it is prohibited to derive benefit for the sake of an eiruv, «and the Rabbis,» who prohibit making an eiruv with such items.

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: מאי טעמא
moves.summary: Rav Aḥa asks Rav Ashi why the mishna's Egyptian ladder does not diminish the wall
moves.about: why an Egyptian ladder does not diminish the wall's height

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לא שמיע לך
moves.summary: Rav Ashi cites Rav via a tradent chain: an object movable on Shabbat does not diminish
moves.about: the Egyptian ladder is movable on Shabbat and so does not diminish

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, אפילו צורי נמי
moves.summary: If so, a Tyrian ladder should not diminish either
moves.about: if movability is the reason, a Tyrian ladder should also not diminish

moves.cueHe: התם כובדו קובעו
moves.summary: A Tyrian ladder's weight fixes it in place
moves.about: a Tyrian ladder's weight fixes it in place

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: כותל שבין שתי חצירות
moves.summary: Abaye: ladders on either side of a wall within three handbreadths of each other diminish it

moves.cueHe: ולא אמרן אלא דלא הוי כותל ארבעה
moves.summary: The three-handbreadth limit applies only if the wall is under four wide
moves.about: Abaye's three-handbreadth limit applies only to a wall less than four wide

moves.cueHe: אמר רב ביבי בר אביי: בנה איצטבא על גב איצטבא
moves.summary: Stacked platforms diminish if the lower is four wide or the upper is four and within three

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה: סולם ששליבותיו פורחות
moves.summary: A ladder with disconnected rungs diminishes on the same terms
moves.about: a ladder with disconnected rungs diminishes the wall

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה:
moves.summary: A four-by-four projection with a ladder of any width placed on it diminishes the wall
moves.about: a projection four by four with a ladder placed on it diminishes the wall

moves.cueHe: ולא אמרן אלא דאותביה עליה
moves.summary: Only if the ladder is placed on the projection, not beside it
moves.about: the projection-and-ladder rule applies only when the ladder is placed on the projection, not beside it

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה: כותל תשעה עשר
moves.summary: A nineteen-handbreadth wall needs one projection, a twenty-handbreadth wall two
moves.about: a nineteen-handbreadth wall needs one projection

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: והוא שהעמידן
moves.summary: Only if the two projections are not one directly above the other
moves.about: two projections permit a twenty-handbreadth wall only if not placed one directly above the other

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא: עמוד ברשות הרבים
moves.summary: A stake of any size driven into a four-wide pillar diminishes its area

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אדא בר אהבה: ובגבוה שלשה
moves.summary: Only if the stake is three handbreadths high
moves.about: a stake diminishes the pillar only if it is three handbreadths high

moves.cueHe: אביי ורבא דאמרי תרוייהו
moves.summary: Abaye and Rava: even a stake under three high diminishes
moves.about: a stake diminishes the pillar even if under three handbreadths

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא
moves.summary: Why do Abaye and Rava hold so?
moves.about: the reason Abaye and Rava hold even a low stake diminishes

moves.cueHe: לא משתמש ליה
moves.summary: The top is no longer usable as a level surface

moves.cueHe: רב אשי אמר: אפילו שגבוה שלשה
moves.summary: Rav Ashi: even a three-high stake does not diminish, since one can hang things on it

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: מלאו כולו ביתדות מהו
moves.summary: On your view, what if the pillar is filled entirely with stakes?
moves.about: on Rav Ashi's view, the status of a pillar filled entirely with stakes

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לא שמיע לך הא דאמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Rav Ashi cites R' Yoḥanan on a pit and its embankment
moves.about: a pillar full of stakes is usable by placing something over them, like a pit and its embankment

moves.cueHe: ואמאי, הא לא משתמש ליה
moves.summary: As with the pit, one places something over the stakes and uses it

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: כותל עשרה
moves.summary: A ten-high wall needs a fourteen-handbreadth ladder
moves.about: a ten-handbreadth wall needs a fourteen-handbreadth ladder

moves.cueHe: רב יוסף אמר: אפילו שלשה עשר ומשהו
moves.summary: Thirteen and a bit suffices
moves.about: the minimum ladder length that permits a ten-handbreadth wall

moves.cueHe: אביי אמר: אפילו אחד עשר ומשהו
moves.summary: Eleven and a bit suffices
moves.about: the minimum ladder length that permits a ten-handbreadth wall

moves.cueHe: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע אמר: אפילו שבעה ומשהו
moves.summary: Seven and a bit suffices, standing upright
moves.about: the minimum ladder length that permits a ten-handbreadth wall

moves.cueHe: אמר רב: סולם זקוף
moves.summary: An upright ladder diminishes; a received tradition whose reason Rav does not know

moves.cueHe: אמר שמואל: ולא ידע אבא טעמא
moves.summary: Shmuel supplies the reason: like a platform on a platform
moves.about: the reason an upright ladder diminishes: it is like a platform on a platform

moves.cueHe: אמר רבה אמר רבי חייא: דקלים שבבבל
moves.summary: Babylonian palm trunks need not be fixed; their weight fixes them
moves.about: Babylonian palm trunks need not be fixed

moves.cueHe: ורב יוסף אמר רבי אושעיא: סולמות שבבבל
moves.summary: Babylonian ladders need not be fixed; their weight fixes them
moves.about: Babylonian ladders need not be fixed

moves.cueHe: מאן דאמר סולמות, כל שכן דקלים
moves.summary: Ladders-view entails palms; palms-view does not entail ladders
moves.about: whoever exempts ladders from fixing all the more so exempts palm trunks

moves.cueHe: בעא מיניה רב יוסף מרבה: סולם מכאן וסולם מכאן
moves.summary: Two narrow ladders with straw between them
moves.about: two narrow ladders with straw rungs between them

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אין כף הרגל עולה בהן
moves.summary: The foot cannot climb on straw; does not diminish
moves.about: the foot cannot climb on straw, so it does not diminish

moves.cueHe: קשין מכאן וקשין מכאן וסולם באמצע
moves.summary: Straw on both sides, ladder in the middle
moves.about: straw on both sides with a narrow ladder in the middle

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: הרי כף הרגל עולה בהן
moves.summary: The foot can climb; diminishes
moves.about: the foot can climb, so it diminishes

moves.cueHe: חקק להשלים בכותל, בכמה
moves.summary: How high must grooves completing a narrow ladder be?
moves.about: how high grooves carved to complete a narrow ladder must be

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: בעשרה
moves.summary: Ten handbreadths
moves.about: ten handbreadths

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: חקקו כולו בכותל, בכמה
moves.summary: How high must a fully carved ladder be?
moves.about: how high a ladder carved entirely into the wall must be

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: מלא קומתו
moves.summary: The full height of the wall
moves.about: the full height of the wall

moves.cueHe: ומאי שנא
moves.summary: Why the difference between the two carved cases?
moves.about: why a fully carved ladder needs more height than a carved extension

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: התם מסתלק ליה
moves.summary: A real ladder is easy to climb; carved grooves are not
moves.about: a real ladder is easy to climb, carved grooves are not

moves.cueHe: בעא מיניה רב יוסף מרבה: עשאו לאילן סולם
moves.summary: Does a tree designated as a ladder count as an opening?
moves.about: whether a tree designated as a ladder counts as an opening

moves.cueHe: תיבעי לרבי, תיבעי לרבנן
moves.summary: The dilemma arises according to both Rabbi and the Rabbis

moves.cueHe: תיבעי לרבי: עד כאן לא קאמר רבי התם
moves.summary: Rabbi's shevut leniency may hold only at twilight

moves.cueHe: או דילמא אפילו לרבנן
moves.summary: Even the Rabbis may treat it as an opening with a lion crouching on it
moves.about: whether even the Rabbis would treat the tree as an opening with a lion crouching on it

moves.cueHe: עשאו לאשירה סולם, מהו
moves.summary: Does an asheira designated as a ladder count as an opening?
moves.about: whether an asheira designated as a ladder counts as an opening

moves.cueHe: תיבעי לרבי יהודה, תיבעי לרבנן
moves.summary: The dilemma arises according to both R' Yehuda and the Rabbis

moves.cueHe: תיבעי לרבי יהודה: עד כאן לא קאמר רבי יהודה התם
moves.summary: R' Yehuda's leniency may be limited to eiruv acquisition

moves.cueHe: או דילמא אפילו לרבנן
moves.summary: Even the Rabbis may treat the asheira as an opening
moves.about: whether even the Rabbis would treat the asheira as an opening with a lion crouching on it

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אילן מותר, ואשירה אסורה
moves.summary: Rabba resolves both dilemmas: tree permitted, asheira prohibited
moves.about: a tree is permitted as a ladder, an asheira is prohibited

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב חסדא: אדרבה
moves.summary: On the contrary: the Shabbat-prohibited tree should be prohibited, the asheira permitted
moves.about: the reverse should hold: a Shabbat prohibition should disqualify the tree, an unrelated prohibition should not disqualify the asheira

moves.cueHe: איתמר נמי
moves.summary: An amoraic tradition (Ravin / R' Elazar or R' Abbahu / R' Yoḥanan) supports Rav Ḥisda

moves.cueHe: אילן — פלוגתא דרבי ורבנן
moves.summary: The tree and asheira questions are simply the known tannaitic disputes
moves.about: the tree-as-ladder question is the dispute of Rabbi and the Rabbis

branch.cue: רב נחמן בר יצחק מתני הכי

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: מאי טעמא
